title: Introduce contextual-entropy-indexer and alert heuristics for prefetch paths
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds a lightweight contextual entropy indexer and heuristic alert weighting for prefetch/pipeline paths. Improves observability of token-level prefetch effects and reduces noisy alerts for transient warmups.
description:
Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts and high-cardinality telemetry around prefetch and prefix-warmup activity that obscures real regressions. This PR introduces a compact "contextual entropy indexer" to fingerprint invocation prompt-contexts, attaches entropy deltas to token-phase spans, and layers a heuristic alert-weighting engine so alerts triggered by prefetch/warmup churn are de-emphasized. The change is explicitly scoped to observability: no runtime behavior changes beyond additional light instrumentation and a configurable sampling hook.

What changed (summary):
- Added an entropy indexing library (pkg/observability/entropy_index) that computes a compact 64-bit context sketch and streaming delta per invocation. The index is intentionally small to avoid metric cardinality explosion.
- Instrumented token-phase spans to emit entropy_delta and prefetch_hint tags when a request used the prefetch path. These are exposed as OTEL attributes and as metric labels for rollups.
- Introduced an alert heuristics layer (services/alerting/heuristics) that consumes token-phase histograms + entropy deltas and applies noise attenuation for alerts matching prefetch signatures. Heuristics are configurable via experiments/heuristics.yaml.
- Dashboard: added observability/dashboards/prefetch-entropy-panel.json — a focused dashboard showing "prefetch rate", "entropy-delta distribution per-route", "token-latency split by prefetch_hint", and a time-series of heuristics attenuations applied.
- Tests and sim harness: added prefetched-invocation synthetic traces to eval-harness/prefetch-sim to validate alert dampening under warmup bursts.

Why this is safe: The entropy index is deterministic and uses only hashed context summary (no PII). Instrumentation is additive and sampled by default (5% global, adjustable per-tenant). Heuristics only change alert scoring; they do not suppress telemetry or modify request routing.

Checklist: 
- [x] pkg/observability/entropy_index: go implementation + docs (see README in package)
- [x] Instrumentation added to runtime span emitter (runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go)
- [x] Alert heuristics engine and configuration (services/alerting/heuristics/*)
- [x] Prefetch dashboard JSON and dashboard setup script
- [x] Unit + integration tests for indexer and heuristics
- [x] Performance sanity run (prefetch-sim) and spike replay tested on staging

Testing results (high level):
- Synthetic warmup burst (1000 prefetched traces/min for 10 minutes) in prefetched-sim: baseline alerts reduced by 72% after heuristics compared to control, true-positive regression alerts preserved.
- End-to-end telemetry CPU impact: +0.6% median on telemetry-ingest workers at 5% sampling; estimated p50 overhead per-request for the indexer is ~120µs when enabled unsampled.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/observability/entropy_index/index.go
- runtime/telemetry/token_phase_emitter.go (added attributes entropy_delta, prefetch_hint)
- services/alerting/heuristics/engine.go
- services/alerting/heuristics/config.go
- experiments/heuristics.yaml
- observability/dashboards/prefetch-entropy-panel.json
- eval-harness/prefetch-sim/*.py (synthetic trace generator)
- integration tests/instrumentation/prefetch_entropy_test.go

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we make the default sampling for the indexer tenant-configurable? Suggest exposing via tenant config with a conservative default (5%).
Maya Singh (author): Good call — added tenant override and documented in experiments/heuristics.yaml.
Priya Nair: The alert heuristics look promising but can we add a fallback rule to escalate if entropy_delta correlates with error-rate instead of latency?
Maya Singh: Added correlation check to heuristics (engine.go) — heuristics now auto-escalate when error-rate > 0.5% over window.
Liam OConnor: Dashboard looks good; consider coloring changes for prefetch vs non-prefetch latency bands.
Maya Singh: Updated panel colors and added hover tooltip explaining prefetch_hint semantics.
post_merge_notes: Deployed to staging on 2026-02-23, promoted to prod 2026-02-25 after smoke tests. Ops playbook added at docs/observability/prefetch-entropy-playbook.md. To rollback, disable heuristics via experiments/heuristics.yaml flag or revert sampling to 0%.
rollback_instructions: 1) Set experiments/heuristics.yaml heuristics.enabled: false and deploy config; 2) If immediate telemetry removal required, set telemetry.sampling.entropy_indexer: 0% in tenant config; 3) Revert commit feature/observability/contextual-entropy-indexer if needed.
notes_for_oncall: Oncall should watch alert-weight-adjustments histogram (dash: prefetch-entropy-panel -> heuristics attenuation). If legitimate alerts are being suppressed, set heuristics.override=true for the affected route and escalate. The playbook includes a quick query to surface suppressed alerts for the last 15m.
security_notes: Entropy indexer uses non-reversible hashing and stores only 64-bit sketches. No contextual content is logged or stored. Reviewed by Security (SUP-4421) and approved for deployment.
performance_summary: Prefetch warmup noise reduction: -72% noisy alerts in sim. Telemetry overhead: ~0.6% CPU at 5% sampling. Storage: marginal increase in metric cardinality due to entropy_label but mitigated via bucketing and reservoir sampling.
notes: This PR aims to improve signal-to-noise in SLO alerting for common prefetch/warmup patterns without hiding real regressions. Config knobs exposed so we can iterate on attenuation heuristics per-customer.
tagline: Compact entropy indexing + alert heuristics to reduce warmup noise and surface real regressions
